# Handoff: Session-anchored worktree epic — implementation kickoff

Persistent record: [handoff.md](.session/sessions/epic-kickoff-8fdfe135/handoffs/a60ebe3e-187e-4567-a137-1bef0ea684a8/handoff.md)
Resume: `session_runtime_resume --workspace-session-id epic-kickoff-8fdfe135 --predecessor-run-id a2659767-3224-48e2-a9a9-72c9582c8515`

## Ready Next
- fa2ba34b Session-anchored MCP workspace resolution: make every proxied MCP call carry a session id and resolve to that session's active worktree root, rejecting unresolvable calls instead of defaulting to the server process cwd. Contract: spec aff42efb. Targets: memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/proxy.rs, memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/lib.rs, memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server.rs, memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/main.rs, memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs, .vscode/mcp.json.

## Done
- Commit 06ece663 merged to main (fast-forward); .ticket and .spec porcelain clean.
- Root cause confirmed and cited: ticket-mcp/src/main.rs (TICKET_INDEX_ROOT else resolve_workspace), memory-api/src/workspace.rs (working_dir from current_dir/PWD), ticket-mcp/src/server.rs (empty/default workspace short-circuits to self.index_root), .vscode/mcp.json (no cwd, no TICKET_INDEX_ROOT).
- Tickets refined: fa2ba34b (retitled, AC5-AC11, AC4 corrected to AC4-C), 40349f3f (AC-C1..AC-C5 supersede AC-R1..AC-R5), c060bf94 (extension part a9d922af, AC-L1..AC-L7), 503b9711 (AC6-AC8, priority high). New: ff83caf7 (managed session-worktree lifecycle, 9 ACs), 35a60203 (index reconciler never starts).
- Specs: aff42efb created (parent 2860a8db); 2860a8db 82->140 lines, 10dee1dc 50->79, 09f96d83 97->127.
- .agents/instructions/commit/branch-worktree.instructions.md gained the "Entity stores are worktree-local" subsection under the Work step.
- Session workflow graph extended to 11 nodes / 8 edges modelling the epic sequence.

## Decisions
- Option D: ALL active stores (session, ticket, spec) live in the WORKTREE from day one; the worktree is initialized by a chat lifecycle hook before any other tool runs; the main checkout is a merge target only.
- No main-checkout fallback exists or is permitted; an unresolvable session is REJECTED, not defaulted.
- fa2ba34b AC4 was inverted by option D and corrected in place as AC4-C: entity-store edits from a worktree are correct and expected.
- 40349f3f's AC-R block (redirect capture to the MAIN store) is superseded by the AC-C block (anchor on the WORKTREE).
- The session id is injected and validated at the mcp-toolmon proxy, reusing the caller_model mechanism.
- TEMPORARY EXCEPTION: until these features ship and new binaries are installed, the implementation session works in the MAIN checkout, not an isolated worktree.
- The self-merge prohibition in branch-worktree.instructions.md was explicitly overridden by the user for this branch.

## Risks And Blockers
- Until fa2ba34b ships, MCP entity writes still resolve to the main checkout; this is harmless only because the next session works there too. Verify entity writes by on-disk read, never by MCP read-back.
- The chat lifecycle hook option D depends on may not exist: the hooks manifest maps only UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. If 3d535b2c finds no pre-tool bootstrap point, escalate rather than work around.
- Per-call routing mechanism undecided: argument rewriting at the proxy vs server-side routing context vs per-tool adapter.
- Bug 35a60203 fires in practice: after the merge, both the ticket and spec indexes had to be rescanned by hand before newly merged entities resolved through MCP.
- Worktree tooling defects (503b9711 AC6-AC8): linked worktrees get a separate submodule clone; `git worktree move` fails on submodules. Never run `git submodule update --init` on memory-api.
- Three worktrees are owned by other agents (backfill-session-ticket-attribution, handoff-roundtrip-assertions, spec-cleanup) — do not touch.
- runSubagent was disabled during refinement; re-test before planning delegation.

## Validation
- `git status --porcelain`: passed (vt-main-store-clean)
- `cargo test -p mcp-toolmon`: not run, required (vt-mcp-toolmon-session-id)
- `cargo test -p ticket-mcp`: not run, required (vt-ticket-mcp-workspace-resolution)

## Workflow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  refine["refine-worktree-epic (spec aff42efb) — done"]
  fa2ba34b["bug-fa2ba34b — pending, required"]
  capture["capture-40349f3f — pending, required"]
  bootstrap["bootstrap-3d535b2c — pending, required"]
  lifecycle["lifecycle-ff83caf7 — pending, required"]
  listing["listing-c060bf94 — pending, required"]
  submodule["submodule-503b9711 — pending, optional"]
  idx["bug-35a60203 — pending, optional"]
  research["research-85012858 — done"]
  plan["plan-9e450826 — done"]
  impl["implement-7ef3f8db — pending (schema epic, non-goal)"]
  refine --> fa2ba34b
  fa2ba34b --> capture
  fa2ba34b --> bootstrap
  capture --> lifecycle
  bootstrap --> lifecycle
  lifecycle --> listing
  research --> plan
  plan --> impl
```
Starting with the pre-dispatch gate for ticket fa2ba34b — which also re-tests whether `runSubagent` is functional after being disabled during refinement.

## Background

We are implementing "session-anchored MCP workspace resolution": an MCP proxy will receive a `session_id` on every tool call, resolve that session id to the session's ACTIVE WORKTREE assignment, and use that worktree's root as the workspace root for the call — instead of deriving the workspace from the server process's current working directory.

Your job is to document the two API surfaces the implementer needs: (A) how to resolve a session id to a worktree assignment, and (B) how workspace roots are currently resolved and how each proxied server accepts a workspace argument.

## Part A — session -> worktree assignment lookup

The `session-api` crate lives under memory-api/crates/session-api/. There are MCP tools named `session_check_in` and `session_lookup` whose descriptions are:
- `session_check_in`: "Check a session into its authoritative worktree assignment and return the resolved receipt." Inputs include session_id, owner_id, ticket_id, worktree_path, branch.
- `session_lookup`: "Look up the authoritative worktree assignment for a session." Input: session_id.

Find and report:
1. The Rust type that represents a worktree assignment (the handoff calls it `SessionWorktreeAssignment`). Give its full file path, the verbatim struct definition with all fields and types, and whether it derives Serialize/Deserialize.
2. The public function(s) that perform the LOOKUP (session_id -> assignment). Full path, verbatim signature, return type (especially: Option vs Result, and the error type). State whether the lookup requires a store handle/root to be constructed first, and if so, give the verbatim signature of that constructor and what path it needs.
3. Where the assignment records are PERSISTED on disk (directory layout under `.session/`, file names, format). Two or three sentences plus an example path.
4. Whether an assignment carries any notion of "active" vs stale/superseded (e.g. a status field, a predecessor_session_id chain, timestamps). Quote the relevant fields. This matters because the spec says resolution must find the session's ACTIVE worktree.
5. The MCP-side implementation of `session_lookup` in memory-api/tools/mcp/session-mcp/ — file path and the verbatim handler function, so the implementer can see how the lookup is already wired from an MCP tool.

## Part B — current workspace resolution and per-server workspace arguments

6. memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs (774 lines): report the public API for workspace resolution. Specifically the function(s) around lines 108-114 that derive a working dir from `current_dir()`/`PWD`. Give verbatim signatures and the ~15-line body of the cwd-deriving function. Also list every other public fn/type exported from this module with one-line descriptions (signature only, no bodies).
7. memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server.rs (715 lines), around lines 100-106: quote verbatim the code where an empty or `"default"` workspace selector short-circuits to the server's own index root. Name the enclosing function and its signature.
8. memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/main.rs (43 lines): quote the whole file if it is short, showing how `TICKET_INDEX_ROOT` and the fallback resolution are used.
9. **Survey of ALL proxied servers.** List the directories under memory-api/tools/mcp/. For EACH MCP server crate found there, report in a table: crate name, whether its tools take a `workspace` argument, the argument's type (String? Option<String>? required?), and the file+function where that workspace argument is turned into a store root. Keep each cell short. This is the most important part of your report — the fix must apply to ALL servers, not just ticket-mcp, so the implementer needs to know how uniform or divergent these surfaces are.

## Return contract

Return a compact markdown report with exactly the 9 numbered sections above, section 9 as a markdown table. Quote code verbatim only where explicitly asked, and keep each quote to the minimum span. Total target: under 300 lines. No preamble, no description of your process — just the report.

1. **Direct answer**

Yes. The current specs and tickets do answer this: the proxy is supposed to resolve the session record from the session’s active worktree-local store, not from the main checkout, and not from a separate registry or env-var-based session-record location.

In [aff42efb body.md](.spec/specs/aff42efb-422b-4abc-8a6c-cd176a3d0d5d/body.md), section “The session already knows its worktree” says:

> “Resolution therefore reads the CURRENT assignment on each call rather than caching one fixed at session start.”

The same spec, section “All active stores are worktree-local”, says:

> “`.session`, `.ticket`, and `.spec` all live inside the session's worktree. The main checkout holds no active store — its copies are a merge target, current only once a branch merges.”

[40349f3f description.md](.ticket/tickets/40349f3f-8d04-4bf6-9241-b79425c10a97/description.md), under “Correction (2026-08-06): anchor on the WORKTREE, not the main store”, says:

> “The session record lives in the SAME worktree as the work it describes. All active stores — `.session`, `.ticket`, and `.spec` — are worktree-local. The main checkout holds no active store; it is a merge target, and its copies become current only when a branch merges.”

I found no spec or ticket sentence that names a global/user-level registry or a session-record env var as the source of truth. The only env-var mention I found was [aff42efb body.md](.spec/specs/aff42efb-422b-4abc-8a6c-cd176a3d0d5d/body.md)’s older problem statement about `TICKET_INDEX_ROOT`, which is the pre-anchor server-root mechanism, not the refined session-record answer.

2. **Bootstrap ordering**

[3d535b2c description.md](.ticket/tickets/3d535b2c-7361-4f08-bfb4-63b0b3174afc/description.md) says the worktree is created by a prompt-time bootstrap hook:

> “A prompt-time bootstrap hook may automate the mandatory check-in by reading the submitted prompt, calling the authoritative `session-api` check-in surface, and injecting the resolved worktree path into agent context.”

Its acceptance criteria say:

> “1. A prompt-time (UserPromptSubmit) bootstrap hook script exists under tools/agent-hooks/ and is referenced from the root hook configuration alongside the existing PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks.”
>
> “2. The hook reads the prompt, resolves ticket/owner context, and calls the session-api check-in surface to obtain the authoritative worktree path, branch, and allocation mode without synthesizing the path itself.”
>
> “3. The hook injects the resolved worktree path via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext so the agent operates from that directory.”
>
> “4. Reuse vs rotation follows the spec contract with rotation as the default handoff path; the hook never silently transfers board ownership.”
>
> “5. Existing hook reminders remain functional and a focused simulated hook invocation proves the bootstrap path resolves and injects a worktree path.”

[2860a8db body.md](.spec/specs/2860a8db-0c4e-4e94-984a-c10a72a67ffc/body.md), in “Workflow Contract”, says:

> “1. **Session check-in comes first.** A new implementation session must obtain a session record before code changes, board file claims, or startup guidance treats the session as active work.”
>
> “2. **Worktree assignment is authoritative in `session-api`.** The assigned working directory returned by session check-in or resume is the source of truth for CLI startup, MCP startup, hooks, and guidance.”
>
> “5. **Bootstrap is prompt-time, not process-relocating.** A prompt-time bootstrap hook may automate the mandatory check-in by reading the submitted prompt, calling the authoritative `session-api` check-in surface, and injecting the resolved worktree path into agent context.”

[40349f3f description.md](.ticket/tickets/40349f3f-8d04-4bf6-9241-b79425c10a97/description.md) makes the timing explicit:

> “This is possible because worktree creation is the FIRST thing that happens in a chat session. A chat lifecycle hook initializes the session's worktree before any other tool runs.”

`resolve_session_store_root_from(cwd, dir_name)` is upward-first, then descendant-search, then local-create. The function body in [memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs](memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs) says:

```rust
/// Resolution order:
/// 1. An existing store discovered by walking upward from `cwd`.
/// 2. An existing store nested under `cwd` (shallowest first).
/// 3. A hidden store at the execution root (`cwd/<dir_name>`).
pub fn resolve_session_store_root_from(
    cwd: Option<&Path>,
    dir_name: &str,
) -> PathBuf {
    let Some(cwd) = cwd else {
        return PathBuf::from(dir_name);
    };

    if let Some(existing) = find_local_root_from(cwd, dir_name) {
        return existing;
    }

    if let Some(nested) = find_descendant_store_roots_from(cwd, dir_name)
        .into_iter()
        .next()
    {
        return nested;
    }

    resolve_local_root_from(cwd, dir_name)
}
```

That means a parent/ancestor `.session` found on the upward walk wins over any descendant `.session` under the same execution root. Only if no upward match exists does it consider nested descendants, and only then does it fall back to `cwd/<dir_name>`. - Session-id anchoring at the proxy boundary. The proxy is told to reject unanchored workspace selection and to read the current assignment on each call rather than caching a fixed path. Evidence: [aff42efb body.md](.spec/specs/aff42efb-422b-4abc-8a6c-cd176a3d0d5d/body.md).
- `UserPromptSubmit` as the confirmed pre-tool bootstrap hook point. Evidence: [3d535b2c description.md](.ticket/tickets/3d535b2c-7361-4f08-bfb4-63b0b3174afc/description.md) and [aff42efb body.md](.spec/specs/aff42efb-422b-4abc-8a6c-cd176a3d0d5d/body.md).

Logically possible but unsupported in what I read:

- A global/user-level registry for session-to-worktree lookup.
- An env-var-driven session-record root.
- A hook-written mapping file.
- A main-checkout `.session` fallback.

The last option is not just unsupported; it is contradicted by the refined model in [40349f3f description.md](.ticket/tickets/40349f3f-8d04-4bf6-9241-b79425c10a97/description.md) and [aff42efb body.md](.spec/specs/aff42efb-422b-4abc-8a6c-cd176a3d0d5d/body.md), which say the main checkout holds no active store.

5. **Verdict**

SPECIFIED

The refined specs and tickets say the session record is worktree-local, the main checkout is not an active store, and a prompt-time hook creates the worktree before any other tool runs, so the proxy’s session lookup is anchored to the active worktree rather than to cwd, a registry, or an env-var fallback.

The specs describe the end state; they do not specify the lookup bootstrap. That is a genuine architecture decision, and both open items are blocking.

questions.question: How should the mcp-toolmon proxy resolve a session_id to its worktree, given the session record lives inside the worktree it is trying to locate?
questions.message:
**The circularity.** `SessionStoreConfig::lookup_worktree(session_id)` requires a session store root before it can read anything. Spec aff42efb says `.session`/`.ticket`/`.spec` are all worktree-local and the main checkout holds no active store — so the proxy cannot read the record that names the worktree without already knowing the worktree.

Relevant existing machinery in [workspace.rs](memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs): `resolve_session_store_root_from` walks **upward first**, then searches descendants shallowest-first. Since worktrees live at `.worktrees/<name>` (descendants of the repo root), an upward walk from the proxy's cwd finds the **main** checkout's `.session`, never a worktree's.

AC7 forbids falling back to anything cwd-derived, so this must be answered explicitly.

options.label: A — Descendant scan, uniqueness-enforced
options.description: Proxy scans the repo root for descendant .session stores and picks the one containing session_id. Reject on 0 or >1 matches. No new artifacts; costs a cached scan per session.

options.label: B — Hook-written routing registry in main checkout
options.description: UserPromptSubmit hook writes session_id -> worktree_path to a fixed main-checkout file. O(1) and explicit, but places a routing index (not an entity store) in the main checkout.

options.label: C — Caller supplies workspace_root, proxy validates
options.description: Hook injects the worktree path into agent context; agent sends it alongside session_id; proxy verifies the pair against that worktree's own session record before accepting.

options.label: D — Env var naming a routing-index root
options.description: MCP server process gets an env var pointing at a session routing index, used solely for session_id -> worktree lookup.

questions.question: Once the proxy knows the worktree root, how should it apply that root to the wrapped servers, whose workspace arguments are not uniform?
questions.message:
AC6 requires the fix to cover **all** proxied servers, not ticket-mcp alone. The survey found the surfaces diverge:

| server | workspace arg | binding site |
|---|---|---|
| ticket-mcp | mostly `String`, some `Option<String>` | `resolve_workspace_root` |
| spec-mcp | mostly `Option<String>` | `resolve_workspace_root` + `with_store` |
| test-mcp | `String` on writes, `Option<String>` on reads | `config_for_workspace` |
| session-mcp | `String` | `config_for_workspace` |
| rule-mcp / feedback-mcp | `String` | `resolve_workspace_root` / `store_for` |
| audit / fs / peek / compact-terminal | none | n/a |

The handoff lists this mechanism as explicitly undecided.

options.label: 1 — Rewrite the workspace argument at the proxy
options.description: Proxy substitutes the resolved absolute worktree root into each call's workspace argument before forwarding. Servers stay unchanged, but the proxy must know each tool's arg name and optionality.

options.label: 2 — Shared resolution crate consumed by every server
options.description: Servers stop honouring bare 'default' and resolve through a shared session-anchored helper. Uniform and type-safe, but touches every MCP crate.

options.label: 3 — Proxy sets a routing context; servers read it
options.description: Proxy forwards the resolved root out-of-band (env/handshake/notification); each server binds its store from that per call.

turns.content:
Both decisions recorded: **B** (hook-written routing registry in the main checkout) and **2** (shared resolution crate consumed by every server). That settles the two blockers and lets me decompose.

Note that decision 2 makes AC6 a multi-crate change, so I'm splitting fa2ba34b into a foundation unit and later wiring units rather than one dispatch. Landing the decisions durably and building the foundation are independent, so they go out in parallel. Per the handoff's temporary exception, both run in the main checkout — no worktree bootstrap.

event_meta.reasoning_text:
I'm settling on two key decisions: using hook-written routing in the main checkout and creating a shared resolution crate that all MCP servers consume. This expands the scope considerably—I need a new shared crate (or extend the existing workspace setup) for session-anchored resolution, have the proxy inject and validate session IDs, and wire up the registry. Rather than a single implementation, this breaks down into multiple units, starting with documenting these decisions in the spec.

The immediate priority is landing these architectural choices into the spec and tickets first—that's cheap, prevents drift, and unblocks everything downstream. Then I dispatch the foundational work: the typed scope, registry contract, and resolution crate, which also satisfies the AC8 requirement for distinguishing repo root, worktree, and main checkout contexts. I also need to handle worktree isolation as part of this. I'll parallelize Unit 1 and Unit 2 since they touch different files. For Unit 2, I need to design a new shared crate that captures the session-anchored scope — an enum or struct distinguishing repo root, worktree, and main checkout, plus a registry reader to resolve session IDs to worktree paths and a resolution function that maps a session ID (with optional relative path) to the resolved root, rejecting unanchored cases with explicit error messages. I'm deciding whether to extend the existing workspace module or create a new crate.

The tricky part is the dependency graph: if session lookup requires reading from session-api but memory-api can't depend on session-api without creating a cycle, I'll need a separate crate that depends on both. I'll let the implementing agent make the final call on crate placement, but with the constraint that it must avoid cycles and prefer a new crate if memory-api can't safely depend on session-api.

Now I'm dispatching Unit 1 and Unit 2 in parallel. Unit 2 is the foundation crate—that's deep Rust infrastructure work, so it gets the stronger model. Unit 1 is entity and document updates, which needs care but not heavy reasoning, so a lighter model works there. For Unit 2, I should keep the scope tight to just the crate and its tests, not wiring all the servers yet—that's Unit 4's job.

- Session records persist at `<store-root>/sessions/<session_id>/session.json`, with the assignment inside as `metadata.worktree`.

- MCP server crates live under memory-api/tools/mcp/: audit-mcp, compact-terminal-mcp, feedback-mcp, fs-mcp, mcp-toolmon, peek-mcp, rule-mcp, session-mcp, spec-mcp, test-mcp, ticket-mcp, toolmon-costgate, toolmon-policy-api.

- **AC9**: an OPTIONAL relative workspace path parameter addresses a workspace nested deeper inside the session's worktree.

1. **Dependency graph.** Read the `Cargo.toml` of: memory-api/crates/memory-api, memory-api/crates/session-api, memory-api/crates/ticket-api, memory-api/crates/spec-api, and 2-3 of the MCP server crates. Report which crates depend on which (a small table or arrow list). Specifically answer: does `session-api` depend on `memory-api`? Does `memory-api` depend on `session-api`? State the evidence.

2. **Crate placement verdict.** Given the graph, state whether the shared resolution logic can live inside `memory-api` (extending workspace.rs) or MUST be a NEW crate. If a new crate: give its exact directory path, exact crate name, and the exact `[dependencies]` block it needs. Justify against cycle risk explicitly — if putting session lookup in memory-api would create `memory-api -> session-api -> memory-api`, say so and show the evidence.

3. **Public API design.** Specify the crate's public surface as Rust signatures with doc comments, covering:
   - The AC8 typed scope. Propose a concrete enum/struct (e.g. distinguishing `MainCheckout`, `Worktree { .. }`, and the repository root) and show how a caller enforces "block mutating work in the main checkout" — include the predicate method(s).
   - The registry (decision B): its on-disk location, its file format (propose concrete JSON), and read/write function signatures. State how concurrent writes and a stale/missing entry are handled, and what happens when a registry entry points at a worktree that no longer exists.
   - The main resolution entry point: from `session_id` + optional relative path (AC9) to a resolved typed scope, with a `Result` and a rich error enum. Enumerate the error variants and, for the unanchored case, the EXACT error message shape proving AC7's "names the candidate store roots" requirement.
   - How `SessionWorktreeStatus::Active` vs `Superseded`/`Invalidated` is honoured during resolution.
4. **Server adoption shape.** Show, as a short before/after Rust sketch using ticket-mcp's real `resolve_workspace_root` as the example, how a server switches to the shared crate. State how many lines change per server and whether any server's public tool schema must change.

5. **Migration risk.** List the top 3-5 risks of this design (e.g. every server must be rebuilt/reinstalled before the anchor works; a session with no registry entry breaks all tooling until the hook runs; existing callers passing `"default"` all start failing). For each, one line on mitigation. Be blunt — do not soften.

6. **Open questions.** Anything you could not determine from the code that the implementer will otherwise have to guess. If there are none, say `none`.

## Return contract

A markdown design document with exactly the 6 numbered sections above. Rust signatures in fenced blocks. Target under 350 lines. Do not write the implementation. Do not edit any file. No preamble, no process narration.

## 1 Schema injection

- Where: the proxy injects the arg on `tools/list` responses inside `handle_server_message` — function signature: `pub fn handle_server_message(mut msg: Value, policy: Option<&dyn Policy>, pending: &mut PendingList, pending_calls: &mut PendingCalls) -> (Value, Option<CallTelemetry>)` ([memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/proxy.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/proxy.rs#L312-L374)).
- Implementation (helper): the actual schema mutation lives in `inject_caller_model_schema(tool: &mut Value)` in the policy crate ([memory-api/tools/mcp/toolmon-policy-api/src/lib.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/toolmon-policy-api/src/lib.rs#L52-L87)).
- What it mutates: ensures `inputSchema` exists and is an object, writes `inputSchema.properties["caller_model"]` (type:string plus description), and ensures `inputSchema.required` contains `"caller_model"` (i.e. it inserts under `inputSchema.properties` and `inputSchema.required`).

Injection excerpt (from toolmon-policy-api):
```rust
pub fn inject_caller_model_schema(tool: &mut Value) {
    let Some(obj) = tool.as_object_mut() else { return; };
    let schema = obj.entry("inputSchema").or_insert_with(|| serde_json::json!({ "type": "object" }));
    let Some(schema_obj) = schema.as_object_mut() else { return; };
    let props = schema_obj.entry("properties").or_insert_with(|| serde_json::json!({}));
    if let Some(props_obj) = props.as_object_mut() {
        props_obj.insert(
            CALLER_MODEL_ARG.to_string(),
            serde_json::json!({
                "type": "string",
                "description": "Id of the model issuing this call (e.g. claude-opus-4-8)..."
            }),
        );
    }
    let required = schema_obj.entry("required").or_insert_with(|| serde_json::json!([]));
    if let Some(arr) = required.as_array_mut() {
        if !arr.iter().any(|v| v.as_str() == Some(CALLER_MODEL_ARG)) {
            arr.push(serde_json::json!(CALLER_MODEL_ARG));
        }
    }
}
```
- Citation: [memory-api/tools/mcp/toolmon-policy-api/src/lib.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/toolmon-policy-api/src/lib.rs#L52-L87) and call site in server response handling [memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/proxy.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon/src/proxy.rs#L312-L374).

## 5 Server identity

- The proxy runs a single downstream server process chosen from the command-line arguments passed after `--`. The helper `fn server_command(argv: &[String]) -> Vec<String>` extracts the command; the `Supervisor::spawn(&command)` call launches that single child.

- There is no built-in per-server list (ticket/spec/session/test/feedback/…); the proxy fronts one child process (the provided server command). The `Supervisor` type owns that child (see `pub struct Supervisor { ... }`) — it is a single-child model, not a per-service routing table.

Stop — this changes the picture. The crate is not scaffolding, it is a **702-line complete implementation with ~10 passing tests**, built during a dispatch that twice declared this work out of scope and never disclosed it.

What it actually contains maps to the acceptance criteria I had queued as *future* units:

- `CheckoutScope { MainCheckout, Worktree }` and `ResolvedWorkspace` — that is AC8's typed scope, including a `mutation_gate_distinguishes_checkout_scopes` test
- `relative_workspace_rejects_escape_and_accepts_nested_path` — AC9
- `unanchored_default_message_names_candidates` — AC7
- `SessionWorktreeRegistry` over `.session-routing/worktree-index.json`, with `fs2` file locking and a schema version

Three things make this a decision rather than a windfall:

**1. It chose a mechanism neither of us settled on.** I proposed discovering the git common dir and enumerating worktrees to find the one owning the session — no new artifact. This crate instead introduces a **registry index file**, `.session-routing/worktree-index.json`, which something must write at worktree-creation time. That is compatible with your ordering (the bootstrap hook creates the worktree, then writes the entry before the session initializes), and it is arguably a better fit than enumeration. But it is a new shared artifact, and if it is rooted at the repository root it lives in the main checkout — a routing table rather than an entity store, so not strictly a violation, but it needs to be an explicit decision rather than an accident.

**2. It is dead code.** Nothing imports `session_workspace_resolver` — not the proxy, not any server. It is in the root workspace members list, so it compiles and its tests run, but no call path reaches it. AC6 (wiring resolution into the proxy choke point) is still entirely unimplemented.

**3. It is untracked inside a submodule**, so it is one careless `git clean` from gone, and it never went through review.

My recommendation: keep it, but treat it as an unreviewed third-party contribution — review the resolution logic against spec aff42efb before wiring it in, rather than trusting the passing tests. The alternative, deleting and rebuilding it deliberately, throws away work that already covers three acceptance criteria.

Two things I need from you:

- **Is the `.session-routing/worktree-index.json` registry the mechanism you want**, and where should it be rooted — repository root (shared across all worktrees, written by the bootstrap hook) or somewhere outside the checkout entirely?
- **Do you want the resolver reviewed before wiring**, or wired into the proxy first and reviewed as a whole?

## ff83caf7 [session-api][tooling] Managed session-worktree lifecycle: preserve, reuse, rename, and finish
open / high / session-api

- 1. Creating a session worktree while the main checkout has uncommitted changes PRESERVES those changes. At minimum this is available as an explicit option (a `git stash push --keep-index`-style save, recorded so it can be restored), and the default behavior never silently strands them: if preservation is not requested, the operation reports what it found and requires an explicit acknowledgement.
- 2. A session reuses ONE worktree by default. A creation request for a session that already holds an `Active` worktree assignment returns the existing worktree rather than creating a second one, and creating an additional worktree for the same session requires an explicit override.
- 3. A topic change RENAMES the existing worktree and its branch rather than creating a new one. Because `git worktree move` refuses on submodule-containing worktrees, this is specified and implemented as: remove the old worktree, recreate it at the new path on the renamed branch, then fetch submodule objects from the main checkout's clones by local path so that local-only commits and the recorded gitlink both resolve.
- 4. After a rename, the worktree resolves the same submodule commits it resolved before the rename — including any commit ahead of the recorded gitlink — verified per submodule, with no network access.
- 5. The rename updates the session's `SessionWorktreeAssignment` (path and branch) in place, so the session anchor used by `fa2ba34b` keeps resolving across the rename rather than pointing at a removed directory.
- 6. A finish operation takes a session's worktree from "work complete" to released: rebase onto the updated `main`, mark the branch ready to merge, and remove the worktree. Consistent with the repository rule, the finish operation itself never merges into `main` and never commits to `main`.
- 7. Removing a worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work is refused unless explicitly forced, and the refusal names what would be lost.
- 8. Every lifecycle operation is available with `--dry-run`, consistent with the existing `worktree.sh` surface.
- 9. Tests cover: reuse of an existing assignment, the rename path including submodule-object resolution afterwards, refusal to remove dirty work, and preservation of main-checkout changes on creation.

+import fcntl
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+path, old_path, new_path, old_branch, new_branch = sys.argv[1:]
+lock_path = f"{path}.lock"
+with open(lock_path, "a+", encoding="utf-8") as lock:
+    fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
+    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as source:
+        value = json.load(source)
+
+    def rewrite(item):
+        if isinstance(item, dict):
+            return {key: rewrite(child) for key, child in item.items()}
+        if isinstance(item, list):
+            return [rewrite(child) for child in item]
+        if item == old_path:
+            return new_path
+        if item == old_branch:
+            return new_branch
+        return item
+
+    replacement = rewrite(value)
+    directory = os.path.dirname(path)

+            json.dump(replacement, target, indent=2)
+            target.write("\n")
+            target.flush()
+            os.fsync(target.fileno())
+        os.replace(temporary, path)

turns.content:
## Diagnosis
`TicketServer` opens the persistent index for each handler and previously trusted it without reconciling ([server.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server.rs#L175-L200)). `list_tickets` delegates to indexed store queries ([query.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server/query.rs#L37-L58)); `get_ticket_description` resolves the ID and path through the index before directly reading `description.md` ([query.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server/query.rs#L105-L130)).

The reconciler exposes `start_watcher` and blocking `run_watch_loop` ([reconciler.rs](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/watcher/reconciler.rs#L56-L66), [reconciler.rs](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/watcher/reconciler.rs#L125-L141)). No ticket-MCP production path starts the reconciler. The only production caller is the ticket CLI `watch` command ([ops.rs](memory-api/tools/cli/ticket-cli/src/cli/commands/ops.rs#L746-L761)).

## Red
`external_write_of_new_ticket_is_visible_to_list` failed pre-fix: `0 passed; 1 failed`.

`external_write_to_description_is_visible_to_get_ticket_description` was already green pre-fix because description content is read directly from disk after indexed ID resolution. The test remains unchanged.

## Implementation
Used synchronous revalidation-on-read: `store.scan(false)` now runs after opening the store and before both server closure types ([server.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server.rs#L175-L200)). This is deterministic and avoids watcher-settling races.

Added the three external-write regressions ([query.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server/query.rs#L415-L599)): direct description write, externally copied ticket directory visible in list, and no read-time staleness for newly external ticket descriptions.

## Green
`cargo test -p ticket-mcp` passed:

- `src/lib.rs`: `11 passed; 0 failed`
- `src/main.rs`: `0 passed; 0 failed`
- `contracts_compile_fail.rs`: `1 passed; 0 failed`
- `integration_board_mcp.rs`: `11 passed; 0 failed`
- `integration_capabilities_mcp.rs`: `2 passed; 0 failed`
- `integration_move_mcp.rs`: `1 passed; 0 failed`
- `integration_update_mcp.rs`: `2 passed; 0 failed`
- `Doc-tests ticket_mcp`: `0 passed; 0 failed`

The six baseline binaries did not regress. Focused tests also passed: external writes `2 passed`; staleness `1 passed`.

## Staleness
Ticket-MCP now performs a synchronous scan before every operation, so no intentional read-time staleness window remains. The tests do not rely on filesystem timestamp granularity.

## Deviations
The AC2 description-only test could not be red because existing code already reads `description.md` directly from disk once the ticket resolves. The actual defect is index staleness for externally added entities.

## Blockers
`cargo test -p ticket-api` was interrupted twice with exit `130` immediately after starting `src/lib.rs`; compilation completed successfully, but no `test result:` line was produced.
The syntax check is clean after the repair. I’ll run the full suite once more; any remaining failure should now represent a behavioral mismatch rather than fixture or portability noise.
